cards.headline:
Ai2's LitPivot refines research
ideas against the literature
cards.body: Ai2's LitPivot helps researchers refine early research ideas with literature-backed critiques and suggested revisions.

blocks.x: Encountering a new paper can change a research idea's trajectory. Ai2 calls this a literature-initiated pivot, and with collaborators at the University of Pennsylvania it built LitPivot to help researchers navigate these pivots.

Using papers retrieved through Asta Paper Finder, LitPivot splits a proposal into its problem, contribution and evaluation plan, groups related papers around the facet being edited, offers critiques backed by excerpts, and suggests revisions researchers can accept, edit or reject.

blocks.cap: LitPivot workflow: select a proposal facet, choose papers, review a supported edit, and refresh the literature as the idea changes.

blocks.x: When one facet changes, LitPivot flags passages that may need revision, such as an evaluation plan that no longer fits a revised contribution.

In a study with 17 researchers, domain experts rated ideas developed with LitPivot as better grounded in the literature than those developed with a text editor and an AI chat tool. Participants also perceived their revised ideas as more novel and useful.

blocks.cap: A researcher refines a proposal about synthetic medical notes into checking contradictions across multiple hospital visits.

blocks.x: LitPivot will be presented at UIST 2026 in Detroit.
